ORG.description: BINTI Rising Initiative is a registered community-based organisation (CBO) in Nairobi, Kenya, empowering young women aged 15-25 through four program pillars: sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and wellbeing, financial freedom and literacy, and women's leadership.

staffRoles.responsibility: Oversees all four program pillars, ensuring quality delivery and alignment with community needs.

staffRoles.title: Monitoring & Evaluation Lead
staffRoles.responsibility: Evidence-based programming through rigorous data collection and impact measurement.

staffRoles.title: Finance & Admin Lead
staffRoles.responsibility: Financial systems, compliance and administrative operations with transparency.

programs.name: Sexual & Reproductive Health Rights
programs.seoTitle: SRHR Program in Nairobi for Young Women
programs.summary: Comprehensive education on sexual and reproductive health, body autonomy, consent, family planning, and access to health services. Empowering young women with knowledge to make informed decisions about their bodies and health.

sessions.title: Understanding Your Body
sessions.desc: Anatomy, puberty changes, menstrual health, and hygiene management for young women.

sessions.title: Consent & Boundaries
sessions.desc: Understanding personal boundaries, recognizing consent, and saying no with confidence.

sessions.title: Family Planning Methods
sessions.desc: Overview of modern contraceptive methods, effectiveness, and accessing reproductive health services.

sessions.title: STIs & HIV Prevention
sessions.desc: Comprehensive education on sexually transmitted infections, prevention strategies, and testing.

sessions.title: Pregnancy & Maternal Health
sessions.desc: Antenatal care, nutrition during pregnancy, and safe delivery practices in Nairobi.

sessions.title: Gender-Based Violence Awareness
sessions.desc: Recognizing GBV, understanding legal protections, and knowing where to get help.

sessions.title: Body Image & Self-Esteem
sessions.desc: Building positive body image, resisting harmful beauty standards, and self-acceptance.

sessions.title: Accessing Health Services
sessions.desc: Navigating Nairobi's health facilities, understanding patient rights, and health insurance options.

outcomes: Programme target: increase SRHR knowledge from a 40% baseline to 80%
Programme target: improved utilisation of reproductive health services
Programme target: enhanced ability to recognise and report GBV
Programme target: better menstrual health management practices
Programme target: increased confidence in accessing health facilities

programs.name: Mental Health & Wellbeing
programs.seoTitle: Mental Health Support Program in Nairobi
programs.summary: Building mental resilience through stress management, emotional regulation, self-care practices, and creating safe spaces for young women to discuss their mental health challenges without stigma.

sessions.title: Understanding Mental Health
sessions.desc: What mental health means, common conditions, and breaking stigma in our communities.

sessions.title: Stress Management
sessions.desc: Identifying stress triggers, practical coping techniques, and relaxation exercises.

sessions.title: Emotional Regulation
sessions.desc: Recognizing emotions, healthy expression techniques, and building emotional intelligence.

sessions.title: Self-Care Practices
sessions.desc: Creating daily self-care routines, mindfulness, and prioritizing mental wellbeing.

sessions.title: Building Support Systems
sessions.desc: Identifying trusted people, building healthy relationships, and knowing when to seek professional help.

sessions.title: Resilience & Goal Setting
sessions.desc: Bouncing back from adversity, personal visioning, and setting achievable life goals.

outcomes: Programme target: improved mental wellbeing scores from a 30% baseline to 70%
Programme target: reduced stigma around mental health discussions
Programme target: established personal self-care routines
Programme target: stronger peer support networks
Programme target: increased willingness to seek professional help

programs.name: Financial Freedom & Literacy
programs.serviceType: Financial literacy training for young women
programs.summary: Equipping young women with practical financial skills including budgeting, saving, entrepreneurship, and income generation. Building pathways to economic independence and breaking cycles of poverty.

sessions.title: Financial Literacy Basics
sessions.desc: Understanding money, income vs. expenses, and why financial knowledge matters for women.

sessions.title: Budgeting & Money Management
sessions.desc: Creating personal budgets, tracking spending, and making smart financial decisions.

sessions.title: Saving Strategies
sessions.desc: Different saving methods, joining chamas (savings groups), building an emergency fund.

sessions.title: Entrepreneurship Basics
sessions.desc: Identifying business opportunities in Nairobi, writing a simple business plan, and starting small.

sessions.title: Understanding Credit & Loans
sessions.desc: How loans work, responsible borrowing, avoiding debt traps, and building credit history.

sessions.title: Income Generation & Networking
sessions.desc: Multiple income streams, leveraging networks in Nairobi, and digital financial tools like M-Pesa.

outcomes: Programme target: regular saving habits rising from a 20% baseline to 65%
Programme target: participants start income-generating activities
Programme target: improved financial decision-making skills
Programme target: formation of peer savings groups (chamas)
Programme target: greater economic independence and confidence

programs.name: Women Empowerment & Leadership
programs.summary: Developing leadership skills, self-advocacy, community engagement, and confidence building. Preparing young women to take on leadership roles in their communities and beyond.

sessions.title: Self-Advocacy & Communication
sessions.desc: Speaking up confidently, assertive communication, and expressing needs effectively.

sessions.title: Women's Rights & Legal Framework
sessions.desc: Understanding constitutional rights, gender equality laws, and legal protections for women in Kenya.

sessions.title: Leadership Skills Development
sessions.desc: Different leadership styles, team building, decision-making, and conflict resolution.

sessions.title: Community Engagement & Civic Participation
sessions.desc: Getting involved in community development, understanding local governance, and civic duties.

sessions.title: Gender Norms & Equality
sessions.desc: Challenging harmful stereotypes, promoting gender equality, and creating inclusive spaces.

sessions.title: Mentorship & Paying It Forward
sessions.desc: Becoming a mentor, sharing knowledge, and creating lasting impact in Nairobi communities.

outcomes: Programme target: leadership competency scores rising from a 25% baseline to 70%
Programme target: increased participation in community decision-making
Programme target: stronger self-advocacy and communication skills
Programme target: formation of peer mentorship networks
Programme target: greater awareness of women's legal rights

communities.name: Kayole
communities.description: A densely settled residential estate in Embakasi East, home to many young families and a vibrant youth population within reach of Nairobi's industrial job market.

communities.name: Mawanga
communities.description: A growing settlement area in the Embakasi side of Nairobi where residents balance informal-sector livelihoods with limited access to youth services.

communities.name: Dandora
communities.description: Known countrywide for its solid-waste dumpsite, Dandora is a resilient community where environmental health burdens fall heaviest on women and girls.

communities.name: Kasarani
communities.description: A fast-growing sub-county along Thika Road mixing planned estates with informal settlements, with a large population of school-leavers and young mothers.

communities.name: Embakasi
communities.description: A major residential and industrial area east of the CBD, where many young women work in informal trade and manufacturing around the Outer Ring corridor.

communities.name: Mathare
communities.description: One of Nairobi's largest informal settlements, where access to sexual and reproductive health information and psychosocial support remains limited for adolescent girls.

communities.name: Kariobangi
communities.description: A mixed estate and informal settlement area neighbouring Dandora, with active women's groups and a strong culture of table banking.

communities.name: Kibera
communities.description: Africa's largest urban informal settlement, where young women lead many of the community's own responses to health, education and economic challenges.

communities.name: Mukuru kwa Njenga
communities.description: Part of the Mukuru informal settlement belt along the Nairobi--Mombasa road corridor, with an active process of resident-led planning and upgrading.

communities.name: Korogocho
communities.description: A high-density settlement next to the Dandora dumpsite, where community organisations play a central role in girls' safety and education.

communities.name: Umoja
communities.description: A bustling middle-density estate whose name means unity, with numerous self-help groups and a strong base of young women entrepreneurs.
